summary: Uma Chakravarti is a historian and Buddhist studies scholar. She studied at Mount Carmel College, Miranda House, Banaras Hindu University, and the University of Delhi under D. Devahuti, later serving as an educator at Miranda House from 1966 to 1998.

Umakant Premanand Shah was an Indologist and historian. He was deputy director (1954) and head of the Ramayana Project (1965) at the Oriental Institute, Vadodara, and director at Maharaja Sayajirao University of Baroda (~1965–1975).

Umar Rolf von Ehrenfels was an Indologist and religious studies scholar. He completed his Ph.D. at the University of Vienna (~1933–1937), became Head of Anthropology at the University of Madras (1949), and was Guest-Professor at Heidelberg University (1961).
Umberto Norsa was an Indology scholar who studied law at the University of Bologna (~1884–1888). He later served as secretary at the Gabinetto di Lettura di Mantova from 1893 to 1938.

Umesh Kumar Singh is an Indology scholar. He completed his B.A. at the University of Allahabad (1997–2000), his M.A. at Banaras Hindu University (2000–2002), and his Ph.D. at the University of Delhi (2004–2010).

Umesha Mishra was an Indologist and philosopher who studied under Helmuth von Glasenapp. He worked at the University of Allahabad (~1923–1956), co-founded Ganganatha Jha Kendriya Sanskrit Vidyapeetha (1943), and directed the Mithila Institute (~1951–1961).

Unapane Pemananda is a scholar of Buddhist and religious studies who earned degrees at USN, Oslo, Peradeniya, and HKU. He held a post at the University of Oslo (2025) and is a guest researcher at PGIPBS (attested 2026).

Unnikrishnan Payyappallimana studied at Bharathiar, Ayurveda College Coimbatore, Amsterdam, and Yokohama National University. He held positions at FRLHT (1995–2007), United Nations University (2010–2020), and became Professor at The University of Trans-Disciplinary Health Sciences and Technology in 2020.

Unrai Wogihara was an Indologist and Buddhist studies scholar who studied at Taisho University and Strasbourg under Ernst Leumann and Junjirō Takakusu. He served as professor at Shukyo University (1907–1926) and Taisho University (~1926–1937).
Unsho Shaku was a Buddhist studies scholar who studied at Mount Koya in 1844 and taught Ekai Kawaguchi. He founded the Juze-kai in 1884, as well as Kairitsu Gakko and Juuzen Hokutsu.

Unuwaturabubule Mahinda is a Buddhist studies scholar who earned degrees from Oriental Studies Society, Buddhist and Pali University, Sri Jayewardenepura, and Kelaniya. He served at Sri Jayewardenepura (2015–2018) and became Senior Lecturer at Buddhist and Pali University (2026).

Uranchimeg B. Ujeed is a scholar of Buddhist and Iranian and Central Asian studies. She earned her Ph.D. from SOAS University of London and served as a Research Associate in the Mongolia and Inner Asia Unit at Cambridge.

Uranchimeg Tsultem is a Buddhist studies and art history scholar. After studies at MNUAC, Eötvös Loránd University, and UC Berkeley (Ph.D. ~2009), she held posts at MNUAC, UC Berkeley, IUPUI, and the Herron School of Art and Design.

Uranchimeg Tsultemin works in art history, Buddhist studies, and Tibetology. She earned a Ph.D. from the University of California, Berkeley, and held posts as Lecturer at UC Berkeley and Associate Professor at the National University of Mongolia.

Urs App is a scholar of Buddhist studies, religious studies, and sinology who earned his Ph.D. at Temple University. He served as Associate Director at Hanazono University and the International Research Institute for Zen Buddhism from 1989 to 1999.

Usha Nilsson was an Indologist and linguist. She taught Harvey B. Aronson and served on the faculty at the University of Wisconsin-Madison (attested 2001), where she became Emeritus Professor of Languages and Cultures of Asia (attested 2026).

Usha R. Jain is a scholar in linguistics and Indology who studied at the University of California, Berkeley, and taught Jinah Kim. She served as Senior Lecturer Emerita at UC Berkeley (attested 2026) and as RDH at Dr Ritu Punia DMD (2024).
Usharbudh Arya was a scholar of Indology and religious studies. He studied at the University of London (~1965–1967) and held a post at the University of Minnesota Twin Cities (~1967–1973).
Uta Reinöhl is a scholar in linguistics and Indology. She held a post at the University of Cologne in 2018 and was appointed Chair of General Linguistics at the University of Freiburg in 2026.

Ute Hüsken is an Indologist and religious studies scholar. She earned her doctorate at the University of Göttingen under Heinz Bechert (~1989–1995), and served as Professor of Sanskrit at the University of Oslo (2007–2017) and professor at Heidelberg University (2017).
